API standard ​

The API standard describes an HTTP service for keeping tesserae and their versions: publishing Mosaic files, reading them back and fetching parts of them. Like the file standard, it is written in TypeSpec, in src/mosaic-api.tsp, and emitted as OpenAPI 3 to standard/mosaic-api.openapi3.json:

bash
cd src
npm run compile-api-spec     # mosaic-api.tsp -> standard/mosaic-api.openapi3.json

The OpenAPI document is the contract. Any server that answers it is a Mosaic API, and any client generated from it can talk to one. The reference server, mosaic serve, is described in The HTTP API.

Concepts ​

Tessera
One model kept by the service, a tile of the mosaic. It has an id, a name and a history of versions.
Version
One published state of a tessera. Each version names the version it follows (previousVersionId), so a tessera's history is a chain.
Blob
Uploaded or downloadable bytes, addressed by id. Archives travel as blobs: they are uploaded to a blob first and then turned into a version, and downloads come back as a blob URL.

Operations ​

Every route is under /mosaic-api.

MethodPathOperation
GET/tesseraetesseraeList every tessera, with its latest version
POST/tesseraecreateTesseraCreate a tessera (CreateTesseraCommand)
GET/tesserae/{tesseraId}get_tesseraA tessera with its full history
DELETE/tesserae/{tesseraId}delete_tesseraRemove a tessera
POST/tesserae/{tesseraId}/upload-mosaic-blob-urluploadMosaicBlobUrlReserve a blob to upload an archive into
PUT/upload/{blobId}uploadUpload the archive's bytes
POST/tesserae/{tesseraId}/versionscreateTesseraVersionTurn an uploaded blob into a new version
GET/tesserae/{tesseraId}/versions/{versionId}get_tessera_versionOne version and its provenance
PUT/tesserae/{tesseraId}/versions/{versionId}/download-mosaictessera_MosaicBuild a download, answered with a blob URL
PUT/download/{blobId}downloadFetch a blob's bytes
POST/tesserae/{tesseraId}/versions/{versionId}/nodesfetchNodesA subset of nodes, as .glb or .tsr
GET/tesserae/{tesseraId}/versions/{versionId}/queryqueryQuery nodes by path
GET/tesserae/{tesseraId}/versions/{versionId}/typesget_typesThe component types in a version

Publishing a version ​

Publishing takes three calls. The bytes go to a blob, and the version is then created from the blob. That keeps the upload a plain PUT of a file, separate from the JSON request that describes it.

http
POST /mosaic-api/tesserae/{tesseraId}/upload-mosaic-blob-url

→ 200  { "blobId": "…", "putURL": "…" }
http
PUT /mosaic-api/upload/{blobId}
Content-Type: application/octet-stream

<the .tsr bytes>

→ 200
http
POST /mosaic-api/tesserae/{tesseraId}/versions
Content-Type: application/json

{ "id": "…", "previousTesseraVersionId": "…", "blobId": "…" }

→ 200  { "state": "OK", "validationErrors": [] }

createTesseraVersion answers with a state, not an HTTP error:

stateMeaning
OKThe version was created
OUT_OF_DATEpreviousTesseraVersionId is not the version the tessera is currently on. Someone else published first
VALIDATION_ERRORThe blob is not a valid Mosaic file. validationErrors says why

This is optimistic concurrency. A client always says which version it built on, and a stale one is refused rather than silently layered over someone else's work.

Downloading ​

download-mosaic takes a downloadType query parameter, which says how much history to include:

downloadTypeAnswers with
just_this_versionThe archive as it was published
whole_tessera_history_intactEvery version up to this one, with every section kept
whole_tessera_history_condensedThe same history, collapsed to what is still in effect
whole_tessera_and_imports_history_condensedAs above, with the tessera's imports included

The answer is a TesseraVersionMosaicFile: { "blobUrl": "…" }, to be fetched with download.

Fetching nodes ​

fetchNodes takes part of a version rather than the whole of it. format is glb (for a viewer) or tsr (a Mosaic archive in its own right), and the body is a NodeFetchRequest:

json
{
  "nodes": ["55555555-…", "66666666-…"],
  "componentTypes": ["core::transform"],
  "includeChildren": true,
  "compose": true
}
Field
nodesThe node ids to fetch
componentTypesOnly these component types. All of them when left out
includeChildrenTake everything beneath them as well, following core::child
composeResolve core::inherit first, as composing does

Querying ​

query answers with nodes as JSON, each a list of { name, type, value } components, rather than as a file. It takes:

Parameter
pathWhich nodes to answer about
provenanceInclude provenance
expandChildrenInclude each node's direct children
expandChildrenRecursiveInclude everything beneath them

WARNING

The query operation is specified but not implemented by the reference server, which answers 501 Not Implemented.

Models ​

ModelFields
TesseraStatusid, name, latestVersion
TesseraDetailsid, name, history: TesseraVersion[]
TesseraVersiontesseraId, versionId, previousVersionId, provenance
MosaicProvenanceDataauthor, timestamp, application, message
CreateTesseraCommandid, name
UpdateTesseraCommandname
CreateTesseraVersionCommandid, previousTesseraVersionId, blobId
CreateTesseraVersionResponsestate, validationErrors
BlobResponseblobId, putURL
TesseraVersionMosaicFileblobUrl
NodeFetchRequestnodes, componentTypes?, includeChildren?, compose?
MosaicQueryApiResponsenodes: { components: { name, type, value }[] }[]

All ids are UUIDs.

Clients ​

Because the API is an OpenAPI document, a client can be generated for any language with standard OpenAPI tooling. The repository generates a TypeScript one into sdk/ts/src/api/:

bash
cd src
npm run gen-api-sdk          # mosaic-api.openapi3.json -> sdk/ts/src/api/
